messages:
Priya Rao: FYI customer (acme-sre) opened an escalation: streaming responses in Safari stop delivering after ~12-20s, Chrome/Firefox fine. They see partial SSE events then no more data until client reconnects. Ticket #12345

acme-sre: Repro steps: private deployment behind corp TLS-inspect proxy + nginx ingress. Using our dedicated endpoint. Safari (macOS & iOS) shows hanging chunk, network tab shows data arriving in tiny fragments.

Alex Chen: Thanks. Do we know whether the corp proxy is doing any content re-encoding or buffering? Also what's their VPC MTU?

acme-sre: MTU 1500 on their VPC. Corp proxy is a TLS-inspect appliance + inline proxy; customer says they cannot disable it.

Marco Diaz: Common pattern: some proxies coalesce or re-chunk SSE frames, or buffer until a full TCP window/newline. Safari's SSE parser may wait for the event terminator (\n\n) and tiny fragments can make it appear as partial output. Any tcpdump or raw bytes from the ingress?

acme-sre: Uploaded a pcap to the ticket. Here's a minimal curl to reproduce from their network:

```bash
curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  --http1.1 \n  "https://private-rw-infer.company.internal/v1/streams/stream123?model=redwood-small"
```

Jamie Park: Can you run that through the corp proxy locally? Also please try `curl --no-buffer` and `-N` to see if libcurl changes behavior.

acme-sre: With `curl -N` we see more frequent small chunks but Safari still pauses. TCP shows the proxy rewriting chunk sizes and coalescing keepalives into a single packet after ~15s.

support-oncall-bot: New log bundle uploaded: prod-ingress/nginx/2026-03-10/stream-123.tar.gz

Alex Chen: From the pcap: proxy injects a TLS MITM cert and seems to buffer until it reaches roughly 8KB or a newline. That matches observed 12-20s stall on low-throughput streams. Nginx ingress has `proxy_buffering on` by default which can also delay SSE. Two likely causes: ingress buffering + corporate proxy re-chunking.

Marco Diaz: Proposed repro and mitigation steps:
1) Reproduce from inside their network with `curl -N` (they did).
2) Temporarily set `X-Accel-Buffering: no` on our upstream responses and ensure `Cache-Control: no-transform` so TLS proxies avoid re-encoding.
3) Add periodic SSE heartbeat comments every 8s: `: hb\n\n` so proxies see repeated data and won't wait to coalesce.
4) For nginx ingress recommend `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on; proxy_set_header Connection "";`

acme-sre: We can try adding heartbeat, and we'll ask infra to set `proxy_buffering off` on the ingress. They can't change the corporate appliance.

Jamie Park: Also send a small patch on the serving side to emit `: keepalive\n\n` at 8s intervals for dedicated/private customers behind known proxies. We should gate it by customer config.

Priya Rao: Can you paste the minimal header change for the service?

Marco Diaz: Sure snippet we tested:```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform
X-Accel-Buffering: no
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

: keepalive\n\n```

Alex Chen: For customers who cannot change corp proxy, we found `Cache-Control: no-transform` + frequent heartbeats fixed Safari stalling in our lab. Nginx ingress `proxy_buffering off` is ideal. Also watch for MTU differences — larger MTUs reduce number of fragments, lowering the chance of tiny partial frames, but we can't force MTU changes in corp networks.

acme-sre: After adding heartbeats at 8s and `X-Accel-Buffering: no` we saw stable streaming in Safari for 48h. They will make the ingress change as a follow-up.

Priya Rao: Marking resolved for now, moving to post-escalation doc. Action items: (1) Marco to draft KB for SSE behavior behind TLS-inspect proxies (include headers/workarounds), (2) Jamie to add optional keepalive config for private/dedicated customers, (3) Support to notify customer about ingest config change. :white_check_mark:

support-oncall-bot: Incident note created: #INC-2026-321 - SSE Safari stall due to proxy buffering (resolved workaround applied).
